title: Detect Overlapping Date Ranges
description: Find all pairs of room bookings for the **same room** that have **overlapping date ranges**. Two bookings overlap if one check-in is before the other's check-out AND vice versa. Show both booking IDs, the room, and the guest names.
solution_sql: SELECT r1.booking_id AS booking1_id, r2.booking_id AS booking2_id, r1.room_id, r1.guest_name AS guest1, r2.guest_name AS guest2 FROM room_bookings r1 JOIN room_bookings r2 ON r1.room_id = r2.room_id AND r1.booking_id < r2.booking_id AND r1.check_in < r2.check_out AND r2.check_in < r1.check_out ORDER BY r1.room_id, r1.booking_id

test_cases.description: 2 overlapping pairs: Room 101 Alice+Bob (Jan 10-15 overlaps Jan 13-18), Room 102 Dave+Eve (Jan 8-12 overlaps Jan 11-14). Grace+Hank in Room 103 are adjacent (Jan 10 = Jan 10) but NOT overlapping.

hints: Two date ranges [A_start, A_end) and [B_start, B_end) overlap when A_start < B_end AND B_start < A_end — this is the standard interval overlap test.
Use r1.booking_id < r2.booking_id to avoid duplicate pairs (A,B) and (B,A) in the self-join.
explanation: The overlap condition r1.check_in < r2.check_out AND r2.check_in < r1.check_out is the canonical interval intersection test. Room 101: Alice (Jan 10-15) vs Bob (Jan 13-18): 10 < 18 AND 13 < 15 → TRUE (overlap). Room 102: Dave (Jan 8-12) vs Eve (Jan 11-14): 8 < 14 AND 11 < 12 → TRUE. Room 103: Grace (Jan 5-10) vs Hank (Jan 10-15): 5 < 15 AND 10 < 10 → FALSE (touching, not overlapping). Result: 2 conflicts.
